description: Compare each group's average rebate to the mean of the group averages.

b.request: Join fees to orders on fees.orderslink = orders.recordvault (inner join), group by orderslink and orders.ordertune to compute each group's average rebtotal and average (rebrate − feerate)/feerate, then compare each group's average rebate to the overall average rebate defined as the mean of those group averages (not the row-level mean), keep groups above it, and return the top 10 by margin (group average rebate minus the mean of group averages) in descending order, unrounded
b.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT f.orderslink, o.ordertune, AVG(f.rebtotal) AS avg_rebate, AVG((f.rebrate - f.feerate) / NULLIF(f.feerate, 0)) AS avg_ratio FROM fees f INNER JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault GROUP BY f.orderslink, o.ordertune), m AS (SELECT g.*, AVG(avg_rebate) OVER () AS overall_avg FROM g) SELECT orderslink, ordertune, avg_rebate, avg_ratio, overall_avg, avg_rebate - overall_avg AS margin FROM m WHERE avg_rebate > overall_avg ORDER BY margin DESC LIMIT 10

c.request: Linking fees to their orders (`fees.orderslink` = `orders.recordvault`, skipping fees without a matching order), for each orderslink and order type (`orders.ordertune`) combination, what are the average total rebate (`rebtotal`) and the average relative rebate-to-fee gap, (`rebrate` − `feerate`) / `feerate`? Show the combinations whose average rebate is above the overall average rebate, with orderslink, order type, average rebate, average relative gap, and how far above the overall average they are. List the top 10 by that margin, largest first, unrounded. Compare each group's average rebate to the mean of the group averages.
c.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT f.orderslink, o.ordertune, AVG(f.rebtotal) AS avg_rebate, AVG((f.rebrate - f.feerate) / NULLIF(f.feerate, 0)) AS avg_rel_gap FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault GROUP BY f.orderslink, o.ordertune), m AS (SELECT AVG(avg_rebate) AS overall_avg FROM g) SELECT g.orderslink, g.ordertune, g.avg_rebate, g.avg_rel_gap, g.avg_rebate - m.overall_avg AS margin_above_overall FROM g CROSS JOIN m WHERE g.avg_rebate > m.overall_avg ORDER BY margin_above_overall DESC LIMIT 10

a.request: Matching each fee record to its order (`fees.orderslink` = `orders.recordvault`, dropping fees with no matching order), group by `fees.orderslink` and order type (`orders.ordertune`), and for each group compute the average total rebate (`rebtotal`) and the average relative rebate-to-fee gap, (`rebrate` − `feerate`) / `feerate`. Take as the baseline the average of these group-level average rebates (each group weighted equally). Return the groups whose average rebate exceeds the baseline, showing orderslink, order type, average rebate, average relative gap, and how much the average rebate exceeds the baseline; sort by that excess, largest first, and show the top 10, without rounding.
a.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT f.orderslink AS orderslink, o.ordertune AS ordertune, AVG(f.rebtotal) AS avg_rebate, AVG((f.rebrate - f.feerate) / NULLIF(f.feerate, 0)) AS avg_relative_gap FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault GROUP BY f.orderslink, o.ordertune), b AS (SELECT AVG(avg_rebate) AS baseline FROM g) SELECT g.orderslink, g.ordertune, g.avg_rebate, g.avg_relative_gap, g.avg_rebate - b.baseline AS excess_over_baseline FROM g CROSS JOIN b WHERE g.avg_rebate > b.baseline ORDER BY excess_over_baseline DESC LIMIT 10

d.request: Linking fees to their orders (`fees.orderslink` = `orders.recordvault`, skipping fees without a matching order), for each combination of orderslink and order type (`orders.ordertune`), what are the average total rebate (`rebtotal`) and the average relative rebate-to-fee gap, (`rebrate` − `feerate`) / `feerate`? Compare each combination's average rebate to the mean of the combination averages (rather than the overall average across all linked records). Show the combinations whose average rebate is above that mean of group averages, with orderslink, order type, average rebate, average relative gap, and how far above the mean of group averages they are. List the top 10 by that margin, largest first, unrounded.
d.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT f.orderslink AS orderslink, o.ordertune AS ordertune, AVG(f.rebtotal) AS avg_reb, AVG((f.rebrate - f.feerate) / NULLIF(f.feerate, 0)) AS avg_gap FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault GROUP BY f.orderslink, o.ordertune), m AS (SELECT AVG(avg_reb) AS mean_avg FROM g) SELECT g.orderslink, g.ordertune, g.avg_reb AS avg_rebate, g.avg_gap AS avg_relative_gap, g.avg_reb - m.mean_avg AS margin_above_mean FROM g CROSS JOIN m WHERE g.avg_reb > m.mean_avg ORDER BY margin_above_mean DESC LIMIT 10
